subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Design structurally sound; leans on machinery already implemented. Root cause confirmed: gate-readiness acceptance trusts frozen submit-time consumer_warnings (gate-readiness.ts:725-730) instead of re-resolving the latest report's typed verification entries against current state.testRuns. The exact-identity typed resolver the design proposes ALREADY exists at report ingestion (verificationWarnings, subagent-report.ts:471-601) with rq-subagentReports25 provenance; the change extracts it into a shared deterministic resolver and ALSO invokes it at acceptance reading state.testRuns[taskId] (mirrored as change.test_runs). changeId identity enforced STRUCTURALLY by workflow isolation (testRuns in ChangeWorkflowState, one per change) - stronger than design prose implies; no cross-change leakage possible. Supersession = latest-report-by-attempt + exact-runId satisfaction (report's own cited runId) so unrelated green run cannot substitute (concern 2). No TDD/adv_run_test widening; non-test policies preserved via existing resolveTaskEvidence/isProofBearingEvidencePolicy (concern 3). 20-entry ring (.slice(-20)) -> undefined lookup -> explicit verification_missing blocker; fails closed (concern 4).

validation.notes: All four asked questions pass structurally. Two execution-phase follow-ups (not design defects): (1) rq-verificationEvidence01 clearing condition (a) wording must be rewritten to define acceptance-time re-resolution so 'warning-free' is unambiguous; (2) add a positive regression that a behavior-bearing TDD task's final report cites a runId still resident in the 20-entry ring (current negative case only proves evicted IDs block). Pre-existing repo note: root-level tools/ and temporal/ duplicate plugin/src/ copies; per AGENTS.md plugin/ is the only shipped code, so implementation MUST edit plugin/src/.

tradeoffs: Acceptance-time live re-resolution vs frozen submit-time warnings: correct, removes false blockers, but acceptance now depends on state.testRuns being current at eval time (mitigated: testRuns is part of same ChangeWorkflowState evaluator already reads -> always consistent).

20-entry ring fails closed correctly, but a TDD-heavy task producing >20 runs before its final report could self-evict the cited runId and block despite legitimate work; design defers ring expansion contingent on regression evidence.

Reusing verificationWarnings resolver at both ingestion and acceptance maximizes locality/single-source-of-truth (P04/P19) but couples the two sites; future resolver changes affect both submit diagnostics and acceptance authority (desirable).

changeId identity is structural (workflow isolation) not a string field; stronger audit boundary but design prose '{changeId, taskId, runId}' triple could mislead a future implementer into adding a redundant/forgeable changeId string compare.

alternatives_considered.option: Recompute and rewrite persisted report consumer_warnings at acceptance (mutate stored report)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Violates audit immutability and re-entry determinism; report is a submission-time artifact. Read-only re-resolution against current state.testRuns preserves frozen report and recomputes authority fresh each eval.

alternatives_considered.option: Trust submit-time consumer_warnings forever (status quo); force re-submit after durable evidence arrives
alternatives_considered.rationale: Observed false-blocker problem; pressures agents to repeat evidence work, produces stale verification_missing. Fails AC1/AC2.

alternatives_considered.option: Accept any latest successful green run for the task (loose 'latest successful')
alternatives_considered.rationale: Directly violates AC3 + design constraint; enables substituting an unrelated run. Exact runId binding mandatory.

alternatives_considered.option: Expand ring buffer beyond 20 as part of this change
alternatives_considered.rationale: Design defers retention expansion as separate work unless regression shows bound blocks normal workflows. Reasonable scope discipline; fail-closed already correct.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to planning/execution. Bake in three corrections: (a) Rewrite rq-verificationEvidence01 clearing condition (a) to define acceptance-time exact-run re-resolution so 'warning-free' is unambiguous; forbid silent grandfathering (already stated). (b) Extract shared resolver, wire into checkUnresolvedVerificationEvidence reading state.testRuns[taskId]; add acceptance-level integration (AC2: earlier-invalid-then-later-valid) AND a positive ring-residency regression for TDD tasks; document >20-run fail-closed UX (re-record/cite resident runId, or typed disposition). (c) Spec/prose: state changeId identity is structural (workflow isolation), explicit match key is {taskId, runId}+exitCode, to prevent a redundant forgeable changeId string compare.

requirement.title: Acceptance Re-resolves Typed Durable Verification Evidence
requirement.body: For a proof-bearing task, acceptance and release readiness MUST evaluate typed verification entries against current task-local durable test-run records, not solely submission-time consumer warnings. The workflow state is the change boundary; within it, a typed entry is valid only when its task ID, cited run ID, and reported exit code match a current record. The latest applicable report attempt may supersede an earlier invalid report only through its own valid cited record. Missing, mismatched, cross-task, or evicted IDs MUST remain explicit blockers. An unrelated successful run MUST NOT substitute for a cited ID.

documents.proposal:
# Fix durable test evidence

## Problem
Acceptance can preserve a `verification_missing` warning captured when an earlier report was submitted, even after a later typed report cites a valid durable `adv_run_test` record. This creates false acceptance blockers and encourages agents to repeat evidence work.

Advance can also pressure agents to create low-value or fake tests for work that is not behavior-bearing code. That adds noise, wastes effort, and can weaken—not strengthen—the evidence record.

## Proposed outcome
1. Make acceptance re-resolve typed verification evidence by the exact `{changeId, taskId, runId}` identity already carried by a report. A valid later report must supersede an earlier invalid report for the same task without allowing an unrelated successful run to satisfy evidence.
2. Lighten evidence expectations where tests are not beneficial or are an anti-pattern, while retaining strong verification for behavior-bearing code.

## Scope
- Test-run recording, report validation, and acceptance readiness for typed durable evidence.
- Task/evidence-policy classification and agent-facing guidance that causes inappropriate TDD or test expectations.
- Regression coverage for valid later evidence after earlier invalid reports.
- Regression coverage proving non-code and non-behavior-bearing work can complete with an appropriate non-test evidence policy.

## Out of scope
- Removing TDD from behavior-bearing implementation work.
- Accepting arbitrary successful test runs as proof.
- Lowering acceptance auditability or allowing unverifiable task completion.

## Guardrails
- Do not broaden TDD or `adv_run_test` requirements.
- Do not require test evidence for non-code deliverables; preserve evidence-policy routes.
- Tests are required only when their executable signal proves behavior-bearing code; use review, static checks, artifacts, source audit, or stakeholder acceptance where those are the correct evidence route.
- Do not use an arbitrary “latest successful” test run as proof.
- Keep missing or evicted referenced runs as explicit, auditable blockers.

## Initial validation
Local tracing found `adv_run_test` records by task/run ID and typed reports match them at submit time, while acceptance evaluates persisted report warnings rather than current durable run evidence. Existing laws already permit non-code evidence policies; implementation and agent instructions may not consistently honor that boundary. This is a durable behavior and auditability change; it needs proposal-sized design and regression coverage.

## Root Cause Analysis
- **Symptom:** an earlier `verification_missing` warning can remain effective after valid durable evidence exists.
- **Cause:** acceptance consumes report-time `consumer_warnings` rather than re-resolving the report’s exact durable run reference.
- **Evidence:** typed report validation uses `test_run_id` / `run_id` exact matching; acceptance readiness examines persisted warnings; test-run storage is bounded to 20 entries per task.
- **Contributing cause:** agent-facing evidence expectations can over-apply test/TDD norms to non-code or non-behavior-bearing work.
- **Safe direction:** preserve exact `{changeId, taskId, runId}` binding; make evidence policy structural and task-appropriate; never substitute a different green run.
- **Risk:** referenced evidence can be evicted by the bounded ring buffer; design must define retention or an explicit blocker path.
documents.problemStatement:
# Problem Statement

Agents can receive an acceptance blocker for missing verification evidence after a valid `adv_run_test` record and typed report exist. The observable failure is a stale `verification_missing` warning surviving from an earlier invalid report.

Agents can also be pressured to create low-value tests for non-code or non-behavior-bearing tasks. That is an evidence-policy mismatch: it produces weak proof and unnecessary work rather than validating delivered behavior.

Expected behavior: acceptance should evaluate the report’s exact durable evidence identity—`{changeId, taskId, runId}`—and allow a later valid typed report to replace an earlier invalid result. It must not treat an unrelated successful run as evidence. Evidence expectations must select the appropriate proof route by task deliverable and behavior risk, not impose red/green tests universally.

## Root Cause Analysis
- **Observed behavior:** acceptance reads persisted report warnings, which may reflect evidence state at report submission time.
- **Expected behavior:** current durable evidence should be resolved against the exact report reference at acceptance.
- **Primary cause:** report warning snapshots are not re-resolved by acceptance readiness.
- **Contributing cause:** task evidence classification and agent-facing guidance can over-apply test expectations.
- **Scope constraint:** retain TDD for behavior-bearing code; do not make non-code or low-risk work manufacture tests.
- **Retention risk:** test-run evidence is retained in a 20-entry task ring buffer, so old referenced records can be unavailable.
documents.agreement:
# Agreement

## Objectives
1. Remove false acceptance blockers caused by stale typed test-evidence warnings.
2. Preserve auditability with exact durable evidence identity at every consumer boundary.
3. Reduce harmful testing pressure by selecting proof based on task deliverable and behavior risk.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a recorded `adv_run_test` result and a typed report citing its returned `runId` for the same change and task, when acceptance evaluates the task, then no `verification_missing` or `verification_mismatch` blocker is emitted for that entry.
2. Given an earlier report for a task has invalid or missing typed test evidence, and a later report attempt cites a valid durable run for that same task, when acceptance evaluates the latest applicable report, then the earlier warning does not block acceptance.
3. Given a report cites a run ID from a different change or task, or a missing/evicted run ID, when acceptance evaluates it, then acceptance remains blocked with an explicit identity or missing-evidence reason; it must not substitute another successful run.
4. Given a non-code task with an allowed non-test evidence policy, when it has the policy’s required evidence, then task completion and acceptance do not require `adv_run_test`, red/green phases, or a test-run ID.
5. Given a behavior-bearing code task using inline TDD, when its evidence is evaluated, then existing exact red/green and typed-run requirements remain enforceable; this change does not weaken them.
6. Automated coverage includes the valid typed-run path and the earlier-invalid-then-later-valid regression path, plus at least one non-code evidence-policy path.

## Constraints
- Evidence proof must be structurally correlated by `{changeId, taskId, runId}`.
- “Latest successful” never means an unrelated green run; it can only mean a later valid report/reference for the same task.
- No new dependencies.
- No widening of `adv_run_test` or TDD requirements.
- Retention loss remains explicit and auditable; no silent fallback.

## Out of Scope
- Removing verification from behavior-bearing code.
- Making acceptance permissive through manual state edits or warning suppression.
- Replacing evidence policies with a one-size-fits-all testing rule.
documents.design:
# Design

## Decision
Acceptance will re-resolve typed verification entries against current workflow `testRuns` using the report’s exact task ID and run ID. `changeId` is structural: each change owns an isolated workflow state, so the effective proof key is `{taskId, runId, exitCode}` within that change.

## Evidence resolution
1. Keep `adv_run_test` recording and returned `runId` unchanged.
2. Keep report-submission warnings as immutable submission-time diagnostics, but do not make those frozen warnings the sole acceptance authority.
3. Extract the existing deterministic typed-entry resolver for shared use by report ingestion and acceptance readiness:
   - Input: task ID, typed verification entry, task-local durable run records.
   - Typed entry: require `test_run_id` / `run_id`; lookup only that ID in that task’s records; compare recorded exit code with reported exit code.
   - Missing, mismatched, or evicted IDs produce explicit blockers.
   - Legacy command-only entries retain compatibility behavior but cannot satisfy the new typed-evidence path.
4. At acceptance, evaluate the latest applicable report attempt for the task using the shared resolver. A later valid typed report replaces an earlier invalid report; an arbitrary later successful run never does.

## Evidence-policy boundary
- Existing typed task fields—deliverable type, evidence policy, and TDD intent—remain the authority for proof routing.
- Non-code tasks using an allowed non-test policy do not require test-run IDs or red/green evidence.
- Behavior-bearing code with inline TDD keeps its existing exact red/green requirements.
- Do not infer a testing obligation from agent prose, task titles, or a desire for coverage. Agent briefs and readiness checks must present the policy-selected proof route.

## Retention
The existing 20-record task ring remains bounded. If a report references an evicted record, acceptance fails closed with a durable, explicit missing-evidence reason. This change does not silently substitute another run. A future retention expansion is separate work unless testing shows the bound blocks normal accepted workflows.

## Regression strategy
- Integration: record an `adv_run_test`, carry returned ID into a typed report, and prove acceptance succeeds.
- Integration: submit an earlier invalid report, then a later valid typed report, and prove only the later applicable evidence governs acceptance.
- Negative: cross-task, missing, mismatched, and evicted IDs remain blocked.
- Policy: prove a non-code task using a valid non-test evidence policy reaches completion/acceptance without `adv_run_test`; prove inline code TDD semantics remain unchanged.

## Spec obligations
Modify `rq-verificationEvidence01` to replace its ambiguous "newer warning-free report" clearing condition with acceptance-time exact-run re-resolution and explicit retention-loss behavior. Update `rq-subagentReports25` only if needed to make the shared resolver’s typed identity boundary explicit. Modify TDD/evidence-policy wording only as needed to make policy-selected non-test proof structural and to prohibit widening test obligations.
